meta.label: Smart thermostats
meta.attribution: Curated from public ENERGY STAR pages, product pages, privacy policies, security notices, smart-home compatibility docs, and independent privacy reviews. HVAC compatibility is house-specific; check wiring, voltage, C-wire, boiler type, region, rebates, and installer requirements before buying. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Sensi Touch 2
products.description: A mainstream ENERGY STAR thermostat with an unusually explicit privacy positioning and broad U.S. HVAC compatibility.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR-certified smart thermostats are independently certified from field data to deliver energy savings; Sensi models appear in the ENERGY STAR thermostat program.

privacy.note: Sensi's public positioning emphasizes data privacy and says Sensi does not sell personal information to third parties.

openness.note: Sensi works through mainstream smart-home integrations rather than an open local-control protocol, so openness is good but not maximal.

transparency.note: Sensi publishes installation, compatibility, privacy, and energy-savings claims in public product materials.

accessibility.note: DIY installation and broad 24V HVAC support help accessibility, but a C-wire may still be required depending on the model and home.

products.name: ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium
products.description: A strong premium option with remote sensors, broad integrations, and better-than-average privacy language for a connected-home product.

environment.note: ecobee markets its premium thermostat around smart energy savings, occupancy sensing, and utility-program participation.

privacy.note: ecobee's privacy notice states that users own their personal information and device data and can manage or delete it.

openness.note: ecobee supports several smart-home ecosystems and voice assistants, which reduces lock-in compared with single-ecosystem thermostats.

transparency.note: Mozilla's privacy review notes ecobee's comparatively strong privacy language while still warning that privacy claims need scrutiny.

accessibility.note: Premium pricing and installation complexity lower accessibility even though the product includes a power-extender kit and rich setup docs.

products.name: tado Smart Thermostat X
products.description: A European smart-heating platform with Matter/Thread support and strong energy-savings claims, best for compatible EU/UK heating systems.

environment.note: tado cites a Fraunhofer Institute report finding up to 28% heating energy savings for tado smart thermostats.

privacy.note: tado's app privacy listing shows location, contact information, identifiers, usage data, and diagnostics may be handled by the app.

openness.note: tado X uses Matter, increasing cross-platform control across iOS, Android, Alexa, Siri, and Google Home ecosystems.

transparency.note: tado publishes support pages for Matter setup and links to terms and privacy policy inside its support system.

accessibility.note: tado X is strong where heating-system compatibility fits, but region, bridge, radiator valve, and subscription-feature choices complicate setup.

products.name: Netatmo Smart Thermostat
products.description: A European smart thermostat with GDPR-region privacy posture and broad assistant compatibility, strongest for compatible boiler systems.

environment.note: Netatmo's energy app and thermostat materials emphasize scheduling and consumption tracking to reduce unnecessary heating.

privacy.note: Mozilla's Netatmo thermostat review highlights GDPR-region protections and notes that Netatmo says it does not sell data.

openness.note: Netatmo publishes HomeKit compatibility support and supports major assistant integrations for its thermostat ecosystem.

transparency.note: Netatmo publishes a dedicated privacy notice for app and product data processing.

accessibility.note: Netatmo is most accessible in compatible European heating setups; regional availability and boiler compatibility can limit fit.

products.name: Google Nest Learning Thermostat
products.description: A polished, recognizable smart thermostat with strong energy features and a major-platform privacy tradeoff.

environment.note: Nest Learning Thermostats are tied to ENERGY STAR certification and Google markets the product around automatic schedules and energy-saving guidance.

privacy.note: Google Home and Nest privacy documentation says Nest device data is handled under Google account and Google privacy systems.

openness.note: Nest supports the Google Home ecosystem and some wider integrations, but it remains heavily tied to Google's smart-home account model.

transparency.note: Google publishes Nest privacy commitments and sensor-use explanations, making the data model more inspectable than many smart-home products.

accessibility.note: Nest is widely available and user-friendly, but HVAC compatibility and Google-account dependence should be checked before purchase.

products.name: Honeywell Home T9
products.description: A familiar room-sensor thermostat with ENERGY STAR certification and broad assistant support, but Resideo account/app dependence.

environment.note: ENERGY STAR lists Honeywell Home T9 thermostat families as certified connected thermostats with demand-response capability.

privacy.note: Resideo's connected-home EULA and privacy statement describe personal data, cookie, service, and product-data processing.

openness.note: Honeywell Home T9 supports Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit, and the Resideo app, reducing single-assistant lock-in.

transparency.note: Honeywell Home publishes T9 product, compatibility, sensor, and ENERGY STAR information on public pages.

accessibility.note: T9 supports common central HVAC systems and room sensors, but compatibility and C-wire/power-adapter needs should be checked.

products.name: Drayton Wiser
products.description: A UK smart-heating platform with strong multi-room and OpenTherm support, useful for boiler homes that want more local heating control.

environment.note: Drayton Wiser cites energy-saving potential from direct boiler modulation, smart control, room-by-room control, and smart modes.

privacy.note: Drayton Wiser publishes a privacy policy and data-protection guidance for smart heating controls.

openness.note: Wiser supports Alexa, Google Assistant, IFTTT, and OpenTherm in supported boiler setups.

transparency.note: Drayton Wiser publishes a security support policy naming support periods and security-reporting channels.

accessibility.note: Wiser is strong for compatible UK boiler systems, but kit selection, hub, TRVs, and installation needs make setup less universal.

products.name: Mysa Smart Thermostat
products.description: A specialty smart thermostat for electric baseboard, fan-forced, in-floor, mini-split, and other nonstandard electric heating/cooling setups.

environment.note: Mysa markets smart scheduling, geofencing, utility demand response, and no-subscription control for electric heating and cooling.

privacy.note: Apple's app privacy label for Mysa lists location, contact, identifiers, and usage data among handled data types.

openness.note: Mysa states support for Google Home, Amazon Alexa, and Apple HomeKit.

transparency.note: Mysa publishes product-family and support documentation by heating/cooling type, which helps avoid buying the wrong voltage class.

accessibility.note: Mysa is unusually useful for line-voltage and mini-split situations, but that specialization means it is not a drop-in fit for ordinary central HVAC.

products.name: Sinope Smart Thermostat
products.description: A Canadian smart thermostat specialist for electric baseboard and other line-voltage heating, strongest when that niche matches the home.

environment.note: Sinope says its baseboard thermostat uses schedules, geofencing, TRIAC control, and time-of-use features to reduce unnecessary electric heating.

privacy.note: Sinope publishes privacy and service links on its storefront, but detailed app-data disclosures are less prominent than some competitors.

openness.note: Sinope product pages show SmartThings and Hilo support and describe ecosystem integrations for the thermostat.

transparency.note: Sinope publishes product specifications and compatibility details for electric baseboard thermostats.

accessibility.note: Sinope is helpful for electric-baseboard homes, but line-voltage compatibility makes it unsuitable for ordinary low-voltage central HVAC.

products.name: Amazon Smart Thermostat
products.description: A cheap ENERGY STAR thermostat for Alexa households, with good affordability and a weak privacy/open-ecosystem fit.

environment.note: The ENERGY STAR product finder lists Amazon Smart Thermostat models as certified connected thermostats with demand-response capability.

privacy.note: Mozilla's privacy review highlights Alexa ecosystem dependence and privacy concerns around Amazon smart-home data.

openness.note: Amazon's thermostat is built around Alexa control and requires the Alexa app, making it a weak fit for open-ecosystem values.

transparency.note: Amazon publishes product, setup, and support materials, but the wider Alexa privacy model is harder to evaluate from a thermostat page alone.

accessibility.note: Low price, ENERGY STAR certification, and DIY setup make this one of the most accessible options for compatible 24V HVAC systems.

products.name: Hive Thermostat Mini
products.description: A UK smart-heating option from Centrica/Hive with a low device price, optional service layers, and a mainstream-platform privacy tradeoff.

environment.note: Hive markets the Thermostat Mini around heating-bill and carbon savings, including app control and smart scheduling.

privacy.note: Hive's privacy policy explains how Centrica Hive collects, shares, and uses personal data for Hive services.

openness.note: Hive works with Alexa and Google Assistant, but it is primarily a Hive/Centrica hub-and-app ecosystem rather than an open local-control system.

transparency.note: Hive publishes product pricing, installation, Hive+ renewal notes, and privacy policy pages for customers to inspect.

accessibility.note: The Mini's low purchase price and UK installer path help accessibility, but hub, pro-install, and optional subscription layers add complexity.

products.name: Wyze Thermostat
products.description: A low-cost thermostat for Wyze smart-home users, but weaker on energy-certification confidence and privacy/open-ecosystem values.

environment.note: Wyze's support page says Wyze Thermostat is not ENERGY STAR approved yet, lowering confidence in verified savings.

privacy.note: Wyze's privacy statement covers account, device, usage, app, and service data across the Wyze smart-home ecosystem.

openness.note: Wyze Thermostat is primarily built for the Wyze app ecosystem plus mainstream assistants, not open local control.

transparency.note: Wyze publishes product and support pages, including a direct answer about lack of ENERGY STAR approval.

accessibility.note: Low price and consumer-friendly setup help accessibility for compatible systems, but privacy and certification tradeoffs remain.
